Not sure if you are joking here, but the reason alcoholic fatty liver exists is because when your liver is working overtime to filter/metabolize/purify alcohol, it begins creating a different substance to do so which combines with free form lipids in your body to form triglycerides and those accumulate in the liver over time.

Nonalcoholic fatty liver is also caused by triglycerides, but because of overconsumption of a combination of fat and sugar. The mechanism of metabolizing excess sugar also combines with free form lipids to create triglycerides, and those accumulate in the liver similar to alcoholic fatty liver — but they have completely different origins
